name: Example: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Secant Function
worked_solution:
The period of $y = \sec x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
\sec{x} = \sec{(x+2n\pi)} .
$$

Substituting $n=4$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sec⁡x & =sec⁡(x+2\cdot 4\cdot \pi ) \\  & =sec⁡(x+8\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\sec{x} = 2\sqrt 2,$ then $\sec{(x+8\pi)} = 2\sqrt 2.$
